# F17b/F17c stale-SOS decision point: ONE scenario set replayed by the iOS store
# test (ios/Tests/IosNativeSosDeliveryStoreTests.swift), the Android guard test
# (android/src/test/.../ProtectionSosStaleGuardTest.kt) and the Dart contract test
# (test/device/own_tag_sos_frame_gate_test.dart). Native is the only classifier:
# the Dart test cannot run either store; it feeds the Dart-path frames as raw
# BLE notifications through BleDeviceRuntimeProvider, answers with the native
# verdicts asserted here, replays the native prompt events into the SDK's
# prompt tracker and checks what Dart does with them (it never classifies).
#
# F17c ambiguous-SOS prompt (DOCS/release/F17C_AMBIGUOUS_SOS_PROMPT.md): ONE
# "unconfirmed stop" record on every platform. Any SDK cancel/resolve of an
# own-TAG SOS seen on any path (native handed over, native countdown, Dart
# forwarded frames) arms it, whatever path saw it, unless native still owes an
# unclaimed create of that SOS. Only the TAG's close frame, a countdown burst,
# the user's answer (send / timeout), a session change or a new SDK SOS end it
# (Roger 16/11/2026: no gap or time cap; a stray retry after any silence still
# asks). A non-burst frame under it is AMBIGUOUS: native asks the user
# (prompt), it never stops the TAG and never drops the frame silently. The 30 s
# native timeout sends the SOS. After "No" the stop is OWED until a GATT write
# of it succeeded (native write result, or Dart's report when Dart owns the
# link): retries meanwhile re-attempt it without asking; once written, a retry
# asks again. F13: a link drop (any path) ends the owed stop: the next retry
# asks again (the TAG may run a new SOS by then).
#
# Line format (plain text: the Android unit-test classpath has no JSON parser):
#   <t_ms> <event> [key=value ...] => <action> [stop=cancel|resolve]
#          [kind=cancel|resolve] [opened=true|false] [prompt=open|closed]
#          [armed=true|false]
# events:
#   seen source=native|native_unclaimed|countdown|dart|none node=N age=MS
#                         what native saw of the SOS before the SDK closed it:
#                         native = its own cycle, handed over (countdown elapsed,
#                         create claimed by the SDK); native_unclaimed = its own
#                         cycle reached its create but the SDK never claimed
#                         it (runtime armed, cycle not handed over); countdown =
#                         its own cycle, countdown still running, started age ms
#                         before the terminal; dart = own-TAG frames that Dart
#                         forwarded (observeOwnTagSosFrame), the first one age ms
#                         before the terminal; none = nothing
#   terminal kind=cancel|resolve node=N connected=true|false [issued=MS]
#                         the SDK's cancel/resolve (closeNativeSosCycle); arms
#                         the record when the SOS was seen on any path.
#                         issued (F17c Phase 2): when the SDK decided that stop
#                         (scenario time). A stop issued before the current
#                         countdown began (native countdown or Dart-forwarded
#                         burst) targets an older SOS: ignored and logged (no
#                         close, no record). Absent: today's behaviour.
#                         target (F17c item 1, Roger 17/11/2026): which native
#                         cycle the stop names. An automated stop (backend
#                         event, portal resolve, reconciliation) carries the
#                         exact native cycle id: target=NAME (an id captured by
#                         cycleid=NAME), default the native cycle id current at
#                         this step. Native applies it only to that cycle: any
#                         other id is ignored and logged
#                         (NATIVE_SOS_STALE_STOP_IGNORED reason=cycle_id_mismatch,
#                         no close, no record) and so is target=none (no id:
#                         the SDK's guard never sends it; reason=no_cycle_id).
#                         target=user: the user's own action (cancel / resolve
#                         button) targets the cycle running now, by definition:
#                         never ignored, no id or issued check.
#                         target=user:NAME (F1, Roger 17/11/2026): the user's
#                         action carrying the native cycle id the SDK captured
#                         at the tap (NAME, captured by cycleid=NAME). Ignored
#                         (NATIVE_SOS_STALE_STOP_IGNORED
#                         reason=user_stop_for_older_cycle, no close, no
#                         record) ONLY when that id is not the current native
#                         cycle id AND the current cycle began after issued:
#                         the user stopped an older SOS, the stop arrived after
#                         a new one began. Otherwise applied as target=user
#   frame node=N source=native|dart [delivered=MS]
#                         one BLE SOS push as delivered by that path; for a
#                         dart frame t is Dart's receivedAtMs and delivered
#                         the native clock when it reached native (default t).
#                         Native counts a Dart frame at its receivedAtMs when
#                         plausible (not in the future, at most 5 s old; never
#                         before the last counted push), else at delivery
#   decide                the 2.0 s decision timer of the open candidate
#   answer choice=sendSos|stopTag|timeout
#                         the user's answer to the prompt (notification action
#                         or app), or the native 30 s timer firing
#   stop_written ok=true|false
#                         the result of the GATT write of the owed stop (native
#                         write callback, or Dart's reportOwnTagSosStopWritten)
#   close source=native|dart [node=N] [code=E1|E2|E3]
#                         the TAG's own close frame 0xE1/0xE2/0xE3 (default
#                         E1), any path; another TAG's close never ends the
#                         record
#   link_drop | link_up [source=native|dart] | session
#                         source=dart: Dart's own link note (noteOwnTagSosLink),
#                         which never resets a burst being counted
#   sdk_open              the SDK opened a new SOS lifecycle (Dart disarms native)
# actions: pass (normal path: not armed / ignored / disarmed; a native-path
#          frame that passes reaches the native cycle: it runs after the
#          step, countdown or SOS, asserted on every platform), pending, duplicate,
#          newSos, prompt (ambiguous: ask the user; opened=true when this step
#          opened the prompt, false while one is already open), stale (the
#          user's "No" is still owed, not yet written: re-attempt it), sosOpened
#          (send / timeout: native opens the SOS through its create), stop (the
#          user's "No": write the matching stop), none, - (no decision).
#          Dart verdicts: pass -> proceed, newSos -> newSos, others -> suppress.
# Asserted keys (absent = default): stop (default none) = the stop written by
# this step; kind = the prompt's terminal; opened (default false); prompt = the
# prompt state after the step; owed = the user's stop still owed after the
# step; armed = the record after the step; cycle=running|idle = the native
# TAG cycle (countdown / handed-over SOS) after the step; cycleid=NAME (F17c
# item 1) = the native cycle id after the step: the first use of NAME captures
# it (it must differ from every id captured before in the scenario: unique per
# cycle), a later use asserts it is unchanged; countdown=T (native-path frames
# only) = after this push the native TAG countdown runs, counted from T (the
# scenario time of the burst's first push: never later, never earlier). A
# platform may start it at the first push or at the push that completes the
# burst; it must run, from T, once the burst is complete.
# Times are ms since the scenario start. Firmware facts: every push arrives
# twice (SOS + TEL characteristic, ms apart); a TAG countdown pushes every
# 500 ms in its first 2 s; an ACTIVE/ACK SOS pushes once per retry
# (2/8/20 s, then 60 s). The same push can also arrive through both paths.

# Case 4b shape: the TAG still runs the SOS after an unconfirmed cancel; no
# answer -> the native timeout sends the SOS (fail safe).
scenario cancel_while_disconnected_then_reconnect_times_out_into_an_sos
0 seen source=native node=7 age=30000 => -
0 terminal kind=cancel node=7 connected=false => - armed=true prompt=closed
1000 link_drop => - armed=true
200000 link_up => - armed=true
230000 frame node=7 source=native => pending
230005 frame node=7 source=native => duplicate
232000 decide => prompt kind=cancel opened=true prompt=open armed=true
240000 frame node=7 source=native => pending
240005 frame node=7 source=native => duplicate
242000 decide => prompt kind=cancel opened=false prompt=open armed=true
261000 answer choice=timeout => none prompt=open armed=true
262000 answer choice=timeout => sosOpened prompt=closed armed=false
320000 frame node=7 source=native => pass armed=false

# F13 (review B2, Roger 18/11/2026): the user's "No" is owed only while the

# ambiguous retry asks again; nothing is stopped automatically.

# F17c review M-D: original H2. The native runtime saw the SOS but its create
# was never claimed by the SDK (not handed over): native still owes that SOS to
# the backend, so the SDK terminal is not a stop of it. No record on any path.
scenario unclaimed_native_create_arms_nothing

# Owner requirement (Roger 16/11/2026): after a TAG-confirmed close (0xE1,
# 0xE2, 0xE3; native and Dart paths) a genuine NEW countdown burst (3 pushes
# within 1.7 s) at +0.5 s, +5 s and +25 s is admitted at once: the native
# countdown starts at the burst's first push, from that push on. ONE rule on
# every platform (F17c M-a): no post-close hold. A lone ACTIVE retry after a
# TAG-confirmed close starts a new SOS at once (owner: an acceptable

# missed is never delayed.

# F17c single stale-SOS decision (Roger 16/11/2026): the real 0xE1 order. The
# TAG closes a sent SOS BEFORE the SDK knows (no SDK terminal yet: the backend
# has not confirmed the cancel, which is still in the outbox) and a new burst
# follows at +0.5 s. The TAG's close is local proof the old SOS is closed: the
# new countdown starts at once from its first push, nothing arms, nothing is
# held. The SDK sends no terminal of the closed SOS to native afterwards (the
# TAG confirmed the close; it would land on the new countdown).
scenario tag_close_e1_before_any_sdk_terminal_native_then_new_burst_at_plus_0_5s

2500 frame node=7 source=native => pass armed=false countdown=1500

# F17c Phase 2 (decided 16/11/2026): the SDK's stop / close carries when it
# was issued. A late stop of an older SOS (A) reaching native after the new
# SOS's (B) countdown began is ignored and logged: B's countdown continues,
# nothing arms. A stop issued for B (after its countdown began) works as
# before; a stop without the field keeps today's behaviour.

# F17c item 1 (Roger 17/11/2026): every SDK stop names the native cycle it is
# for. A = an SOS seen through Dart's link and closed on the TAG (0xE1); B = a
# genuine new TAG SOS whose countdown native opened right after, unseen by
# Dart. A's late automated terminal (portal resolve / backend event decided
# after B's countdown began) names A's cycle: never applied to B, B's countdown
# continues (the issue time alone would not catch it: decided after B began).

# F1 (review af2f32f, Roger 17/11/2026): the user's stop names the native
# cycle in front of them AT THE TAP. The user cancelled A at 50 (0x04 written
# at once, the TAG closed A at 100); B, a genuine new TAG SOS, began natively
# at 1000, unseen by Dart; A's deferred native close lands at 1500. It names A
# and was issued before B began: ignored, B's countdown continues.
